intent.tagline: The tool counts. The judgment names the plan.
intent.narration: A review read the whole corpus and still could not see a smell a command one line of code can count. This design gives the two audit modes one mechanical source and keeps tool output apart from judgment.

problem_solution.problem: Review and maintenance audit a repo with reading and judgment. They run no linter. A smell a tool can count, such as a duplicated block, is invisible to a reading pass.
problem_solution.solution: One script runs habit-sensors through its JSON surface and writes habit-smells.json. Review and maintenance add a Mechanical smells section that names the tool and the branch base, and maintenance trends each pair of smell and file against the previous report.
problem_solution.narration: The script moves data. It never judges. Review classifies the groups and may re-classify with evidence, and it states the unavailable case instead of claiming a clean scan.

beats.text: No report carries a count a tool can name, so a review can miss 930 duplicated-code hits a command prints in one line.
habit-hooks stays an external CLI under ADR-0025, and the script gets no new dependency.
The script records the JSON findings, not the rendered coaching text, so a report can carry and diff them.
A broken tool run can read as a clean scan. An incomplete run is a P1 finding that names the tool.

alternatives.why_not: It is session coaching, not a findings record.
Maintenance needs the first scan as its baseline.
